column2: Rinse the lentils several times until the water runs clear, then drain.
Peel the carrot and dice it small; chop the onion finely.
Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat and fry the onion for 3–4 minutes until translucent.
Add the carrot and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the lentils and water and bring to the boil; skim off the foam on the surface with a spoon.
With the lid ajar, cook over low heat, stirring now and then, for 25 minutes until the lentils break down.
Take off the heat and blend with a stick blender until smooth; keep the blender at the bottom of the pan so it doesn’t splash.
Season with salt to taste; set aside a portion for babies and young children before adding salt.
Wash and drain the rice; chop the onion finely.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the lentils, bulgur, rice and water and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Cook over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn’t stick.
Add the dried mint and boil for 2 more minutes.
If it’s too thick, add hot water and boil for 2 more minutes.
Score the tomato skins, leave them in boiling water for 1 minute, then peel and chop roughly.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until they release their juice.
Add the water, bring to the boil and cook for 10 more minutes over low heat.
Add half the basil and blend.
Serve garnished with the remaining basil leaves.
Wash the rice and put it in a pan with the water; once boiling, cook over low heat for 15 minutes until soft.
For the liaison, whisk the yoghurt, egg yolk and flour in a bowl until smooth.
Take a few ladles of the boiling soup and add them gradually to the liaison to warm it; then pour it into the pan, stirring constantly.
Bring to a gentle boil once, stirring constantly, then turn off the heat; don’t leave it on high heat or the liaison will curdle.
Melt the butter in a small pan, add the dried mint and after 10 seconds drizzle it over the soup.
Put the tarhana in a pan with the cold water and whisk until no lumps remain; leave for 10 minutes.
Bring to the boil over medium heat, stirring constantly so it doesn’t stick.
Once boiling, lower the heat and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Wipe the mushrooms with damp kitchen paper and slice thinly; chop the onion finely.
Melt the butter in the pan and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and sauté for 6–7 minutes until they release their liquid and it evaporates.
Add the water gradually, stirring so no lumps form; once boiling, cook for 10 minutes.
Add the milk and boil for 3 more minutes; blend half of it if you like.
Peel and dice the potato; wash the broccoli and break into small florets; chop the onion.
Add the potato and water, bring to the boil and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the broccoli and cook for 10 more minutes until it is tender.
Peel and dice the courgettes and potato; finely chop the onion and dill.
Add the courgette and potato and stir for 3 minutes.
With the lid ajar, cook over low heat for 20 minutes until the vegetables mash easily with a fork.
Add the dill and boil for 1 minute.
Put the chicken in a pan with the water and bring to the boil; skim off the foam and simmer for 25 minutes until completely white inside.
Take out the chicken and shred it; strain the cooking liquid and leave it in the pan.
Dice the carrot small and add it to the liquid with the olive oil; cook for 10 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Return the shredded chicken and boil for 2 minutes.
Take off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes; serve hot.
Dice the carrot and courgette small; grate the tomato.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and sauté the carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the courgette and tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the orzo and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Chop the onion finely and dice the carrot small.
Add the lentils and water and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and cook the flour for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the water gradually, stirring so no lumps form.
Once boiling, cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and cook the tomato for 5 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and cook over low heat for 8–10 minutes until soft.
Chop the onion finely and dice the carrot and potato small.
Put all the vegetables, the lentils and the water in a pan and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Add the dried mint and stir.
Dice the carrot, potato and courgette small.
Add the carrot and potato to the cooking liquid and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the courgette and cook for 8 more minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Return the chicken and boil for 2 minutes.
Wipe the mushrooms and slice thinly; chop the onion finely.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and sauté for 6–7 minutes until their liquid evaporates.
Add the water gradually, stirring so no lumps form; once boiling, cook for 10 minutes.
Add the milk and boil for 3 more minutes.
Peel and dice the pumpkin, potato and carrot; chop the onion.
Add the vegetables and stir for 3 minutes.
Grate the carrot and add it to the cooking liquid; cook for 10 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken and stir.
Char the aubergines over a gas flame or in the oven for 15–20 minutes until the skins blacken and the flesh is soft.
Once lukewarm, peel the skins and finely chop the flesh with a knife.
Melt the butter in the pan, soften the chopped onion for 3 minutes, add the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the water gradually, stirring so no lumps form.
Add the aubergine and, once boiling, cook over low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the milk and boil for 3 minutes.
Peel and dice the celeriac, carrot and potato small; toss the celeriac with half the lemon juice so it doesn’t discolour.
Bring the vegetables to the boil with 5 cups of water; cook over low heat for 25 minutes until the celeriac is soft.
Whisk the yoghurt, egg yolk and remaining lemon juice.
Grate the tomatoes; peel and deseed the roasted peppers and chop them.
Add the tomato and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water and bring to the boil; cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Bring the orzo to the boil with the water; cook over low heat for 12–15 minutes until soft.
Chop the onion and carrot small.
Sauté the onion and carrot in olive oil in a small pan for 4 minutes and add them to the cooking liquid.
Add the chickpeas and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Peel and dice the potato; break the broccoli into florets and chop the onion.
Put the onion, potato and water in a pan and bring to the boil; cook for 10 minutes.
Add the broccoli and cook for 10 more minutes until tender.
Add the milk and warm over low heat; without boiling, add the kashar and stir until it melts.
Grate the tomatoes, cook them in olive oil for 5 minutes and add to the cooking liquid.
Add the orzo and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Take off the heat and add the lemon juice.
Peel and dice the courgette and potato; chop the onion.
Add the courgette, potato and water and bring to the boil.
Dice the courgettes and chop the onion finely.
Add the courgettes and stir for 3 minutes.
Wash the green lentils and put them in a pan with the water; once boiling, cook over low heat for 20 minutes.
Chop the onion finely and soften it in a separate pan for 4 minutes, dry or with a few spoonfuls of water; add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the onion and tomato paste and the bulgur to the lentils.
Cook over low heat, stirring now and then, for 15–20 minutes until the bulgur and lentils are soft.
Add the carrot and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Peel and dice the carrots and potato; chop the onion.
Add the orange juice and heat without boiling.
Peel and dice the pumpkin and carrot; chop the onion.
Add the ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the pumpkin, carrot and water and bring to the boil.
Char the tomatoes in the oven or a pan for 10–12 minutes until the skins blacken; peel and chop.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the bulgur and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Soak the wheat the night before; drain and put it in a pan with the water.
Once boiling, cook over low heat for 40–45 minutes until the wheat is soft; add hot water if needed.
Halve the leeks lengthways and rinse the soil from between the layers under running water; slice thinly.
Peel and dice the potatoes; chop the onion finely.
Add the leeks and stir for 5 minutes until wilted.
Add the potatoes and vegetable stock and bring to the boil.
Slice the mushrooms; dice the carrot small and chop the onion finely.
Add the mushrooms and carrot and sauté for 6 minutes until the mushrooms’ liquid evaporates.
Peel and deseed the roasted peppers and chop them; grate the tomatoes.
Add the pepper and tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Blend half the chickpeas and return them to the pan; the soup will thicken.
